question:
(a) Obtain the piecewise form of $\tan^{-1}(\tan x)$ for $x\in[0,2\pi]$ wherever the expression is defined.

(b) Hence evaluate $\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ and $\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)$.
explanation:
(a)
The principal-value range of $\tan^{-1}t$ is
$$\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$$
For $0\leq x<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $x$ already belongs to this range. Hence,
$$\tan^{-1}(\tan x)=x$$
For $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$$\tan x=\tan(x-\pi)$$
Therefore,
$$\tan^{-1}(\tan x)=x-\pi$$
For $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$$\tan x=\tan(x-2\pi)$$
Thus,
$$\tan^{-1}(\tan x)=x-2\pi$$
Hence,
$$\tan^{-1}(\tan x)=\begin{cases}x, & 0\leq x<\dfrac{\pi}{2}\\x-\pi, & \dfrac{\pi}{2}The expression is undefined at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ because $\tan x$ is undefined there.

(b)
Since $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\in\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$,
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{2\pi}{3}-\pi=-\frac{\pi}{3}$$
Since $\dfrac{7\pi}{4}\in\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2},2\pi\right]$,
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\tan\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{7\pi}{4}-2\pi=-\frac{\pi}{4}$$
Thus, the required values are $-\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
